newsitem.title: INDIA: India ends agency monopoly of sugar exports.
newsitem.headline: India ends agency monopoly of sugar exports.

text.p: Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma has approved an ordinance to end a private agency's monopoly over sugar exports, the Food Ministry said on Monday.

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's cabinet had earlier this month approved the ordinance, repealing the Sugar Export Promotion Act of 1958 and ending the Indian Sugar and General Industries Import-Export Corp's (ISGIEC) monopoly over exports.
"The President has given assent to the ordinance for decanalisation of sugar export with effect from January 17, 1997," the ministry statement said.
The statement said sugar exporters could register their quota requests with the Agriculture and Processed Foods Export Development Association (APEDA).
The sugar export quota, already released to ISGIEC and STC before the promulgation of the ordinance, would have to be implemented within three months of the order, the statement said.
The government had said in August that it would authorise more firms to export sugar, ending the monopoly held by ISGIEC, an agency set up by private millers.
But a government-backed bill to end the monopoly did not clear parliament before it adjourned in late December.
Deve Gowda told a public meeting in the eastern state of Bihar last month that the ordinance would facilitate the export of 3.5 million tonnes of sugar stocks.
